grammar.title: 正在…(呢) and V著: actions in progress
grammar.pattern: Subject + 正在 + Verb + (Object) + 呢 / Verb + 著
grammar.explanation: 正在 goes right before the verb to say an action is happening at this moment: 我正在吃飯(呢). The particle 呢 at the end makes it sound softer and more spoken. 著 goes right after the verb and describes a state that keeps going, either the state of a thing (門開著) or a second action done 'while' doing the main one (她笑著說). Use 正在 for 'in the middle of doing', 著 for 'is in this state / doing it this way'.
grammar.contrast: 已經…了 is the opposite side: it marks something finished (我已經做完了 = I've already finished), while 正在 marks something still going on (我正在做 = I'm still doing it). If you can add 完, it is 已經…了; if the action is unfinished right now, it is 正在.
grammar.common_error: Learners add 了 to a 正在 sentence, saying 我正在吃飯了. Don't — 正在 means the action is unfinished, so it never takes the completed 了. Also, 著 attaches directly to the verb (坐著看書), never before it.

passage.title: 我的一天
passage.hanzi: 去年我來台北工作,住的房子離捷運站很近。今天早上我正在吃早餐,老闆就打電話來,說有一件事要我今天做完。我在公司做了三個小時,現在已經做完了。下午我騎著腳踏車去附近的書店,買了一本新書,坐著看,覺得很舒服。
passage.gloss: Last year I came to Taipei to work; the place I live is close to the MRT station. This morning, just as I was eating breakfast, my boss called and said there was something he needed me to finish today. I worked on it at the office for three hours, and now it's done. In the afternoon I rode my bike to the bookshop nearby, bought a new book, and sat reading it — it felt really nice.

grammar.title: Three ways to say "help": 幫 / 幫忙 / 幫助
grammar.pattern: A 幫 B + V ／ A 幫 B 的忙 ／ A 幫助 B
grammar.explanation: 幫 is the everyday verb and takes a person directly, usually followed by what you do for them: 我幫你做. 幫忙 is verb + object already ("do a favour"), so it cannot take another object right after it — say 幫我一個忙 or just 幫忙. 幫助 is a bit more formal and works both as a verb taking a person (他幫助新同事) and as a noun (謝謝你的幫助).
grammar.contrast: 幫忙 vs 幫助: if a person follows immediately, you need 幫 or 幫助, not 幫忙. If the person is split out (幫我的忙) or there is no object at all (請你幫忙), use 幫忙. As a noun after 的, only 幫助 works.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 他幫忙我做事情 or 謝謝你的幫忙我. Because 忙 is already the object of 幫, you must say 他幫我做事情 / 他幫助我, and for the noun 謝謝你的幫助.

passage.title: 我們公司
passage.hanzi: 我在一家不大的公司上班。公司就在捷運站附近，騎腳踏車十分鐘就到了。老闆人很好，他常告訴我們：事情太多的時候，別一個人做，可以請同事幫忙。上個週末我身體不舒服，他讓我在家多睡一點；同事還為我做完了那些事情。他們的幫助讓我覺得，公司就是我的第二個家。
passage.gloss: I work at a small company. The company is right by the MRT station — ten minutes by bike and you're there. The boss is a good person; he often tells us: when there's too much to do, don't do it alone, you can ask a colleague for help. Last weekend I wasn't feeling well, and he let me stay home and sleep more; my colleagues even finished those tasks for me. Their help makes me feel that the company is my second home.
